subtitle: Where the Kaveri Turns, a Kingdom Takes Root

panels.shot: wide aerial sweep over the Kaveri looping around sandbanks and buried temple spires
panels.action: Dharmapala of Talakad stands on a high sandy bluff above the wide Kaveri, his cloak whipping in the river wind, half-buried stone shrines and shifting dunes stretching behind him.

dialogue.text: Long before Talakad’s temples lay under sand, the Western Gangas chose this restless river bend as their capital, carving Gangavadi’s fate into earth, stone and water.

i18n.hi: तलाकाड के मंदिरों के रेत में डूबने से बहुत पहले, पश्चिमी गंगों ने इस चंचल मोड़ को राजधानी चुना, गंगवाड़ी की किस्मत मिट्टी, पत्थर और पानी में लिख दी।

panels.shot: slow push-in along the Kaveri’s course, following its glittering surface between wooded banks
panels.action: The Kaveri snakes through a broad alluvial plain, its waters glinting in afternoon light as farmers work fields on both sides and shallow ferries cross between sandy islets.

dialogue.text: In the 5th and 6th centuries, the upper Kaveri basin was neither a legend nor a curse, but a living corridor of fields, ferries and shrines waiting for a court to bind it together.

i18n.hi: पाँचवीं–छठी सदी में ऊपरी कावेरी इलाका न कोई दंतकथा था न श्राप, बल्कि खेतों, नावघाटों और देवालयों से भरा रास्ता, जो दरबार से जुड़ने का इंतज़ार कर रहा था।

panels.shot: wide landscape showing scattered hamlets, a small shrine, and distant low hills
panels.action: Clusters of mud-and-timber houses hug the river edge, smoke rising from hearths, while a modest stone shrine with a simple linga stands on slightly higher ground away from floodwaters.

dialogue.text: Talakad was not born as a grand capital. It began as river hamlets and shrines, shaped by floods, silt and the slow work of farmers who watched the Kaveri’s moods.

i18n.hi: तलाकाड कोई जन्मजात शाही राजधानी नहीं था। वह नदी किनारे की बस्तियों और देवालयों से शुरू हुआ, बाढ़, गाद और किसानों की धीमी मेहनत से, जो कावेरी का मिज़ाज पढ़ते थे।

panels.shot: close-up on Dharmapala of Talakad studying a rough map traced in sand
panels.action: Dharmapala of Talakad kneels on the riverbank, tracing lines in the damp sand with a stick to mark paths, ferries and villages, his brow furrowed in concentrated thought.

dialogue.text: When the Western Gangas looked at this bend in the Kaveri, they saw more than scenery. They saw a node from which Gangavadi-96000 could be reached, ruled and remembered.

i18n.hi: जब पश्चिमी गंगों ने कावेरी के इस मोड़ को देखा, उन्हें सिर्फ़ नज़ारा नहीं दिखा; उन्हें ऐसा केंद्र दिखा जहाँ से गंगवाड़ी-९६००० तक पहुँचा जा सके, राज किया जा सके, याद रखा जा सके।

panels.shot: medium shot, Dharmapala addressing a small council of chiefs under a tree
panels.action: Dharmapala of Talakad stands beneath a large riverbank tree, gesturing toward the water as local chiefs sit on mats, listening with a mix of caution and interest.

dialogue.speaker: the_ganga_court_at_talakad
dialogue.text: Here, the river gathers our lands. Let our court rise where its waters turn.

i18n.hi: यहीं नदी हमारी धरती को समेटती है। हमारा दरबार वहीं उठे जहाँ इसका पानी मुड़ता है।

panels.shot: low-angle view of early construction at Talakad
panels.action: Workers haul stone blocks up from barges, carpenters raise wooden scaffolds, and Dharmapala of Talakad watches from a raised sandy ridge, measuring the line of a future street with his gaze.

dialogue.text: Epigraphic traces tell us the Gangas used more than one seat. Yet Talakad, on the Kaveri’s sand, became a named capital, where the court anchored power in a riverine town.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख बताते हैं कि गंगों की एक से ज़्यादा राजधानियाँ थीं, फिर भी कावेरी की रेत पर बसे तलाकाड को नामदार राजधानी बनाया गया, जहाँ दरबार ने नदी किनारे कस्बे में सत्ता गाड़ दी।

panels.shot: interior wide shot of a newly built wooden-pillared audience hall
panels.action: Inside a long hall of timber pillars and stone base, Dharmapala of Talakad sits on a simple raised seat, scribes beside him as a village headman presents a palm-leaf petition.

dialogue.text: From Talakad, grants were recorded, disputes weighed, and villages along the Kaveri and Nanjangud region folded into Gangavadi-96000, the great unit carved in epigraphic formulae.

i18n.hi: तलाकाड से दान दर्ज हुए, झगड़े नापे गए, और कावेरी किनारे व नंजनगुड के गाँव गंगवाड़ी-९६००० में जोड़े गए, उस बड़े इकाई में जो शिलालेखों के सूत्रों में तराशी गई।

panels.shot: close-up on a stone being chiseled with an inscription
panels.action: A sculptor leans over a dark stone slab, chiseling neat Brahmi-Kannada characters, while Dharmapala of Talakad stands nearby, inspecting the emerging royal grant inscription.

dialogue.text: The Epigraphia Carnatica volumes preserve these voices: Ganga kings granting land, water rights and revenues to temples and brahmanas, naming Talakad as a seat of their authority.

i18n.hi: एपिग्राफिया कार्नाटिका के खंड ये आवाज़ें बचाए हुए हैं: गंगा नरेश मंदिरों और ब्राह्मणों को ज़मीन, पानी और राजस्व देते हुए, तलाकाड को अपनी सत्ता की आसंदी कहते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of temples rising near the river
panels.action: Temple structures with low shikharas rise on slightly elevated ground, priests and artisans moving among carved pillars, while the Kaveri glides by, dotted with boats and sandbars.

dialogue.text: Alongside the court, shrines grew. Ganga patronage etched itself into stone as endowments for lamps, rituals and feeding houses tied temple wealth to the river-fed fields around Talakad.

i18n.hi: दरबार के साथ-साथ देवालयों की कतारें उगीं। गंगा संरक्षण पत्थर पर उतरा–दिये, पूजाओं और भोजनशालाओं के लिए दान, जिसने मंदिर की संपत्ति को तलाकाड के सिंचित खेतों से बाँध दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Dharmapala watching ferries and traders
panels.action: Dharmapala of Talakad stands at a ferry point, watching traders load grain sacks and pottery onto flat-bottomed boats, while men and women cross with baskets on their heads.

dialogue.text: The capital’s promise was practical. Control of ferries, tolls and river routes bound upland villages to Talakad, making the Kaveri not just a boundary, but an artery of power.

i18n.hi: राजधानी का वादा ठोस था। नावघाट, चुंगी और नदी मार्गों पर पकड़ ने पहाड़ी गाँवों को तलाकाड से जोड़ा, कावेरी को सिर्फ़ सीमा नहीं, सत्ता की धमनियों में बदल दिया।

panels.shot: wide seasonal montage of the river plain in flood and in drought
panels.action: In one half of the frame, the Kaveri swells, covering low banks and lapping at temple steps; in the other, the river is shallow, exposing wide sandy stretches and stranded boats.

dialogue.text: Geomorphology work reminds us: the Kaveri shifted. Sands advanced and retreated. Talakad’s story is written in floods, in channels that moved, and in people who adjusted each season.

i18n.hi: भूमिरूप अध्ययन याद दिलाता है: कावेरी बहाव बदलती रही। रेत बढ़ी–घटी। तलाकाड की कहानी बाढ़ों, बदलती धाराओं और हर मौसम खुद को ढालते लोगों में लिखी है।

panels.shot: subtle bird’s-eye view of the town plan hugged by natural levees
panels.action: From above, streets and compounds cluster on slightly higher, firmer ground, with fields and ferry ghats lining the lower banks, showing how settlement chooses its place against the river.

dialogue.text: Archaeological surveys trace old foundations under today’s sands. They show a town that once hugged stable ridges, leaving the most dangerous low-lying stretches to water and silt.

i18n.hi: पुरातत्व सर्वेक्षण आज की रेत के नीचे पुरानी नींवें खोजते हैं। वे दिखाते हैं एक कस्बा जो मज़बूत टीले से सटा था, सबसे ख़तरनाक नीची पट्टियाँ पानी और गाद के लिए छोड़ देता था।

panels.shot: medium shot of farmers reinforcing embankments
panels.action: Farmers and laborers stack woven mats and stone along a small embankment, reinforcing it as the current presses against the bank, while children watch from a safe distance.

dialogue.text: The Gangas’ promise to this landscape meant work: bunds to tame overflow, canals to carry water inward, and grants that tied families to the task of keeping the capital’s fields alive.

i18n.hi: इस धरती से गंगों का वादा काम से जुड़ा था: बाँधों से उफान को रोकना, नहरों से पानी भीतर लाना, और ऐसे दान जो परिवारों को राजधानी के खेतों को ज़िंदा रखने से बाँध दें।

panels.shot: interior shot of Dharmapala at a ritual in a temple
panels.action: Dharmapala of Talakad stands before a linga in a stone shrine, hands folded, as priests conduct a ritual, lamps flickering and carved walls bearing fresh inscriptional bands.

dialogue.text: Inscriptions from Talakad and Nanjangud speak of donations for worship. Through such acts, the court wove rivers, fields and deities into a shared frame called Gangavadi-96000.

i18n.hi: तलाकाड और नंजनगुड के शिलालेख पूजा के लिए दान का ज़िक्र करते हैं। ऐसे कर्मों से दरबार ने नदी, खेत और देवताओं को एक साझा चौखटे—गंगवाड़ी-९६०००—में बुन दिया।

panels.shot: time-lapse style composition showing later layers of building and abandonment
panels.action: The frame shows successive phases: sturdy stone temples, later extensions, some structures collapsing, and new shrines elsewhere as sand slowly creeps over unused walls.

dialogue.text: Centuries passed. Other dynasties rose. Courts moved to Kolar and beyond. Talakad’s prominence waned, yet its stones remained, some maintained, some left to the quiet advance of sand.

i18n.hi: सदियाँ गुज़रीं। और वंश उठे। दरबार कोलार व आगे खिसक गए। तलाकाड की चमक फीकी पड़ी, पर इसके पत्थर रहे, कुछ सँभाले गए, कुछ रेत की शांत चढ़ाई पर छोड़ दिए गए।

panels.shot: low, dramatic shot of partially buried temple spires in modern times
panels.action: Half-submerged temple towers peek out of rippled dunes, with the Kaveri flowing calmly in the background and sparse vegetation clinging to wind-shaped slopes.

dialogue.text: Today, Talakad’s buried shrines invite tales. A later story of Queen Alamelamma’s curse is famous, but it belongs to 17th-century struggles, not to the Ganga court’s founding.

i18n.hi: आज तलाकाड के दबे देवालय नई कहानियाँ बुलाते हैं। रानी अलमेलम्मा के श्राप की बाद की कथा मशहूर है, पर वो सत्रहवीं सदी की लड़ाइयों की है, गंगा दरबार की नींव की नहीं।

panels.shot: close-up on a weathered inscription stone half-emerged from sand
panels.action: A hand brushes sand away from a weathered stone slab, revealing sharp-edged characters that still cling to the rock, illuminated by angled evening light.

dialogue.text: Epigraphers and archaeologists read Talakad differently: not as proof of a curse, but as layered evidence of river shifts, changing settlements and the long memory of Ganga grants.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख-विद और पुरातत्वज्ञ तलाकाड को अलग तरह पढ़ते हैं: श्राप का सबूत नहीं, बल्कि नदी के बदलते बहाव, बदलती बसाहटों और गंगा दानों की लंबी याद का परतदार निशान।

panels.shot: dreamlike blend of Dharmapala overlooking both ancient town and present sands
panels.action: Dharmapala of Talakad stands in the same pose as the cover, but now the scene blends old bustling streets with present-day dunes and exposed shrines, past and present overlapping.

dialogue.text: To found Talakad as a capital was to speak to the river plain: a pledge that law, worship and cultivation would hold here as long as people listened to what the Kaveri itself required.

i18n.hi: तलाकाड को राजधानी बनाना दरिया मैदान से संवाद था: ये प्रतिज्ञा कि कानून, पूजा और खेती यहाँ टिके रहेंगे, जब तक लोग खुद कावेरी की माँग को सुनते रहेंगे।

panels.shot: final wide shot of the Kaveri at Talakad at sunset
panels.action: The Kaveri glows under a red-gold sky, sandbanks and temple spires casting long shadows, the landscape quiet yet marked by human traces along its edges.

dialogue.text: Talakad on the Kaveri sand reminds us: a capital is never just walls and titles, but a long, risky promise made to a landscape that can answer with silt, silence or enduring memory.

i18n.hi: कावेरी की रेत पर तलाकाड हमें याद दिलाता है: राजधानी सिर्फ़ दीवारें और पद नहीं, बल्कि धरती से किया लंबा, जोखिम भरा वादा भी है, जिसे वो गाद, ख़ामोशी या टिकाऊ यादों से जवाब दे सकती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: Where the Kaveri Turns, a Kingdom Takes Root
subtitle_i18n.hi: जहाँ कावेरी मुड़ती है, वहीं जन्म लेती है एक राजधानी
